blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Whole-slide images may contain coexisting lesions, yet weak supervision typically provides only the most severe diagnosis. We formulate this setting as dominant-label multiple instance learning, where the observed label is the maximum-severity element of a latent lesion set. Standard multiclass MIL treats it as a complete one-hot description and therefore suppresses lower-severity evidence whenever it co-occurs with a dominant lesion. We propose DomSet-MIL, a label-aware framework that aligns the annotation mechanism across bag and instance levels. Dominant-Label Censored Likelihood models the reported diagnosis without declaring unreported lesions absent. Severity-Ordered Residual Routing assigns patch evidence from high to low severity and preserves residual support for secondary findings, while top-$q$ pooling links local routing scores to bag prediction. Experiments across natural and controlled settings show that DomSet-MIL achieves state-of-the-art performance in dominant-label prediction while more effectively recovering latent coexisting-lesion evidence. These findings demonstrate that modeling the dominant-label mechanism can improve diagnostic prediction without sacrificing clinically meaningful secondary findings.
blocks.zh: 整个滑坡图像可能含有并存的损伤,但监督不力通常只能提供最严重的诊断。 我们将此设定为主要标签的多实例学习,其中所观察到的标签是潜在损害集的最高强度要素。 标准多级MIL将它视为一个完整的一热描述,因此,每当它与主要损伤共同发生时,都会压制低等证据. 我们提出DomSet-MIL,这是一个具有标签意识的框架,它协调了包和例之间的注释机制。 上报的诊断结果, Severity-Ordered Dreamers Routing将补丁证据从高度到低度分配,并保留了对二级结论的剩余支持,而上-美元集合则将本地的路由分数链接到包预测. 跨越自然和受控制环境的实验表明,DomSet-MIL在主要标签预测中实现了最先进的性能,同时更有效地恢复潜在的并存效应证据。 这些研究结果表明,对主导-标签机制的模型可以改进诊断预测,而不会牺牲临床上有意义的二级发现。

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Whole-slide images (WSIs) provide a comprehensive view of tissue morphology, but
their gigapixel resolution makes dense region-level annotation impractical.
Weakly supervised and multiscale systems address this challenge without exhaustive
region annotations [ 1 , 2 ] ;
multiple instance learning (MIL) [ 3 ] represents a WSI as
patch embeddings learned from one slide-level diagnosis.
Complementary work on zero-shot subtyping uses fine-grained patch–text
alignment to connect local morphology with pathology-aware descriptions,
as in FG-PAN [ 4 ] .

blocks.en:
This mismatch arises when a heterogeneous specimen is summarized by its dominant
finding. A pathology WSI can contain regions with different diagnostic significance [ 11 , 12 ] ,
yet weak supervision may expose only the most severe lesion. The annotation
therefore records the maximum severity of a latent lesion set, rather than the
set itself: a slide containing malignant and atypical tissue is labeled
malignant, so standard softmax treats atypical as an incorrect bag label. Across
such cases, unreported secondary lesions become structural false negatives;
lower-severity labels are censored whenever they co-occur with a more severe
finding, and changing the aggregator cannot remove supervision introduced by
this annotation rule.

blocks.en:
Recent work incorporates diagnostic severity into multiclass MIL. PAMS organizes
classes hierarchically, penalizes clinically costly underestimation, and mixes
features across priorities [ 13 ] , but still targets only the final
diagnosis, so lower-severity evidence need not remain positive. Multi-instance
multi-label methods predict coexisting breast lesions but assume multiple
diagnoses are observed during training [ 11 ] . Learning from a
single positive label relaxes that assumption by leaving other labels unknown [ 14 ] , yet generic
missing-label objectives neither explain why one label was selected nor link
bag-level presence to localized evidence. This gap calls for explicit modeling of the dominant-label annotation mechanism.

blocks.en: We propose DomSet-MIL , a label-aware framework that predicts the dominant diagnosis while preserving evidence for hidden lesions. At the bag level, Dominant-Label Censored Likelihood (DCL) converts a malignant presence gate and a residual atypical gate into three observed class probabilities via the annotation’s maximum-severity rule; a malignant label supervises malignant presence without declaring atypical absence. At the instance level, Severity-Ordered Residual Routing (SORR) applies the rule in descending severity: a malignant gate claims matching patches, an atypical gate processes residual evidence, and unclaimed mass forms the benign remainder. Top- q q pooling connects these severity-specific patch assignments to DCL’s censored bag scores. The two components therefore impose the same severity-ordered factorization at complementary resolutions.
blocks.zh: 我们提出DomSet-MIL, 一个具有标签意识的框架, 在袋子层面,主要标志-Label Censored Viclihood(DCL)通过注释的最大严重程度规则,将恶性存在门和残存的非典型门转换为三个观察到的类概率;恶性标签监督恶性存在而不宣布非典型缺席. 在案例一级,Severity-Ordered remaindal Routing(SORR)在降级严重程度中适用了该规则:恶性门声称有匹配的补丁,非典型门处理残留证据,无声质量构成良性剩余部分. Top-q q 集合将这些针对重度的补丁任务与DCL的审查袋分数联系起来. 因此,这两个组成部分在补充性决议中规定了同样严重程度的阶梯化。

blocks.en:
Our contributions are threefold: (1) We identify lower-severity lesions as
structurally censored under dominant-label supervision, explaining their
suppression as negative classes. (2) We introduce DomSet-MIL, coupling DCL with
SORR to align latent evidence at bag and patch levels. (3) We evaluate
dominant-label prediction and latent-lesion recovery on BRACS [ 12 ] ,
with test-time ROI annotations and on controlled EBRAINS/TCGA mixed-bag benchmarks.

blocks.en:
Tissue is segmented by Otsu thresholding [ 31 ] and tiled into

The projection in Eq. ( 2 ) has dimension 512. We use

and one bag per update for up to 100 epochs. Early stopping uses validation macro-AUC with
a patience of 15 epochs. The pooling fraction is selected from q ∈ { 0.01 , 0.05 , 0.10 , 0.20 } q\in\{0.01,0.05,0.10,0.20\} on the validation set. BRACS results are averaged
over five seeds. Controlled-task results are averaged over folds, five seeds,
and, for TCGA, the class orders.

blocks.en: Three matched controls isolate label modeling from aggregation. Flat-CE uses the shared patch projection and top- q q readout, replacing SORR with competing patch logits and DCL with softmax cross-entropy. CR-Ordinal applies a two-gate continuation-ratio head to a pooled bag representation, without instance-level residual routing. WAN uses independent sigmoid patch heads and the same top- q q readout, training with Cole et al.’s [ 14 ] weak-assume-negative loss, weighting each unreported class by γ = 1 / ( | 𝒞 | − 1 ) \gamma=1/(|\mathcal{C}|-1) .

blocks.en:

blocks.en: On the controlled tasks, each model’s bag-level class scores are compared with the held-out multi-hot indicator of S i S_{i} . Set mean average precision (Set-mAP) is the primary, threshold-free latent-set recovery metric, computed over all classes. Hidden-lesion recall (Hidden-R) is a complementary, threshold-dependent diagnostic computed over pairs ( i , c ) (i,c) for which c ∈ S i c\in S_{i} and c ≺ y i c\prec y_{i} ; singleton bags do not enter its denominator. For Hidden-R only, each method and class uses a threshold selected on the validation set by maximizing F1 against the retained latent sets. This evaluation-only calibration does not enter model fitting or early stopping. Table 2 reports representative attention-, instance-, distillation-, severity-, and state-space-based MIL baselines together with all matched label-model controls. DomSet-MIL leads every table metric. Relative to WAN, the next strongest method, it improves Set-mAP by 0.035–0.038 and Hidden-R by 0.089–0.096 across the three controlled tasks. CR-Ordinal has higher dominant-label M-AUC than WAN on all three controlled tasks. WAN leads in Set-mAP and Hidden-R by 0.077–0.090 and 0.140–0.152, respectively. The two evaluations give opposite rankings for these controls.

blocks.en: 3.4 Ablation study

blocks.en:
We isolate the two factorizations and the pooling operator on BRACS. Replacing
DCL with cross-entropy retains SORR but restores mutually exclusive bag-level
supervision. Replacing SORR with independent class gates retains DCL but removes
residual instance routing. Finally, mean, max, and noisy-OR pooling separately
replace top- q q pooling without modifying the gates or bag-level likelihood.
Table 3 reports both dominant-label performance and secondary-evidence recovery to assess
their trade-offs.

blocks.en: 4 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 4 结论

blocks.en:
We identify a fundamental mismatch in conventional multiclass MIL: a diagnosis
reporting only the most severe lesion censors coexisting lower-severity findings,
which standard training treats as negatives. DomSet-MIL addresses this mismatch
by coupling DCL with SORR and top- q q pooling, aligning dominant-label
supervision with severity-ordered patch evidence. Across natural and controlled
settings, it improves dominant-label prediction and latent or localized
secondary-lesion recovery, while ablations support the complementary roles of
censored supervision, residual routing, and sparse pooling. These results show
that modeling the weak-label generation process enables richer pathological
representations from slide-level annotations. Future work will consider
partially ordered, data-dependent, and uncertain label mechanisms, as well as
whether biomedical knowledge-guided prompts, such as those explored in
MeDKCoOp [ 43 ] , can support lesion-specific evidence learning.

blocks.en: 5 Compliance with Ethical Standards

blocks.en:
This study used only de-identified or coded pathology images from the released
BRACS, EBRAINS, and TCGA resources; no new participants, specimens, or animals
were involved. All data were used in accordance with the applicable access and
data-use terms.
